If, however, there would be anything you'd like to add at this moment, and I invite you not to start any debate with counsel, because you had better have any debate outside of this courtroom, and I also understood that you have had ample opportunity to discuss the matter with counsel, but I would not refrain you from addressing the Chamber if you'd like to do that at this moment. Where I said "the Chamber," I should say the two remaining Judges.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to all. First of all, I wish to thank the Trial Chamber, although there are only two Honourable Judges here, for allowing me to address them. If we use the terminology from economics, I would say that this is a temporary calculation or a sum-up of the trial heretofore. I wish to say only a brief -- a couple of words that would be useful for the continuation or for the future of our trial. You have heard out my counsel Stewart, and of course it is only natural for me to consult with my counsel. I wish to say that I endorse his submissions and I would just briefly like to explain something that might clarify my decision to deny my consent. Your Honours, I have spent a long time in prison here, and it would be only normal for me to wish to end this proceedings as soon as possible, because any further delay is contrary to my interests. But, as Mr. Stewart has said here, I would of course wish to leave the prison tomorrow. However, the proceedings have to take their course. The reason why I opted for a rehearing is only one, but I wish to add to what Mr. Stewart has said. I have followed the proceedings from my perspective, and a great many things have not been clarified here. Although many helpful witnesses have been called here, in a rehearing, these witnesses would shed more light to the events that had taken place in Bosnia-Herzegovina during the war. For this reason, I believe it would be helpful for a retrial to take place, because it could prove to be helpful for all sides; the Defence, the OTP, and the Trial Chamber alike, because it would help expedite the proceeding. Because the start of the trial was rushed, the Defence was unable to prepare sufficiently, and there have been quite a few flaws committed on our part. The Defence would require a longer period of time, which could be beneficial for it, and this could be done in a new trial, where the two of you Honourable Judges would be present, along with a third Judge, and before such trial would start, the Defence would have enough -- ample time to prepare itself. I would turn to another issue that touches upon the fairness of trial. I wish to go back to what Prosecutor Mr. Harmon said. At this stage, the Prosecution would have to use the opportunity to amend the indictment and withdraw a number of allegations that were deemed corroborated before the proceedings reached this stage. Another matter that I would like to mention here, Your Honours, is the following: In the forthcoming period I wish to take an active part in these proceedings, which I have not taken so far. I will abide by your wish not to repeat some of the submissions stated here by my counsel, but I do wish to reiterate my request to put certain questions to witnesses during their testimony here and I would like you to allow me to address this issue at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krajisnik. Because that's a matter which is not to be addressed at this moment, because it's beyond the issue. You're talking now about the modalities of the future conduct of the case, whether that would be after restart or whether it would be after we would have decided to continue that case. And that's something that should be dealt with at that moment and not at this stage. Therefore, your active part is not something to be discussed at this moment. I do understand that --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be allowed, Your Honour, to say only a few words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not on the issue of your active involvement in the case, because that's not a matter to be discussed at this moment. The issue at this moment at stake is the -- whether it's in the interests of justice, whether it would be served or would be better served by continuing rather than to hear the case all over again. That's the limit of what we can discuss at this moment. But at least I do understand that you fully support the position taken on your behalf by Mr. Stewart. Is there any other matter you'd like to bring to our attention?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will only address you with a few more words. I did not wish to discuss here the different reasons why I would like to take an active part in the proceedings. Rather, I wanted to say that in a rehearing, I would have more opportunity to do so. However, by way of conclusion, I would like to say the following: In a new trial, I would have a better chance to prove a number of events and facts that we were unable to prove so far. I am aware of the fact that the final decision lies with the Trial Chamber and the Tribunal, but I am convinced that whatever your decision will be, we will have a fair trial. However, I appeal to you to have the understanding to consider the reasons put forth by us behind our request for a retrial. Furthermore, I would also appeal to you to set aside some time for us to deal with some of the issues that have remained outstanding to this day, like, for instance, the issue of a laptop and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's certainly something that will get proper attention once a decision has been taken, once a final decision has been reached as to whether the case -- the hearing of the case will be continued or that we would rehear the case de novo, as it is said in Latin. If there are no further submissions --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'd only like to say this, that despite Mr. Krajisnik saying that a rehearing would present a better opportunity and take an active part, I nevertheless maintain that submission on his behalf that that's the preferable course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand your position, Mr. Stewart. We will adjourn, as again it's said in Latin, sine die, and the two remaining Judges will consider whether or not it's appropriate to give a decision as they could take under Rule 15 bis (D). We stand adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned sine die
